title: Multiqubit orthogonal product bases
abstract: We study complete orthogonal product bases (OPBs) of an $n$-qubit system via the formal-matrix formalism for multiqubit OPBs. To each OPB formal matrix we associate an edge-colored complete multigraph, and we prove that two formal matrices are equivalent if and only if their multigraphs are isomorphic, thereby reducing the classification of OPBs to graph isomorphism. Via subcube partitions and a lemma of Tarsi, we upper bound the number of variables by $2^n - 1$. We also study lower and upper bounds on the number $a_n$ of equivalence classes of $n$-qubit OPBs, by showing that $\binom{a_{n-1}+1}{2} \le a_n \le B_{2^{n-1}}^n$, where $B_m$ denotes the number of partitions of an $m$-element set. These bounds yield the asymptotic behavior $a_n = 2^{2^{n+o(n)}}$. Finally, we obtain a two-phase algorithm that decides whether two OPB formal matrices are equivalent, together with its correctness proof and complexity analysis. The complexity is exponential in the worst case.
summary: This paper tackles the classification of complete orthogonal product bases (OPBs) for $n$-qubit systems by mapping the problem onto graph isomorphism. The authors prove that equivalence is determined by the isomorphism of an associated edge-colored multigraph. They derive bounds showing the number of such bases grows doubly exponentially and present a complex, two-phase algorithm to test for equivalence.
main_problem: The primary goal is to classify all complete orthogonal product bases (OPBs) for an $n$-qubit system up to natural equivalence.
main_result: The classification problem is reduced to determining the isomorphism of associated edge-colored complete multigraphs, and the number of equivalence classes $a_n$ exhibits doubly exponential growth, $a_n = 2^{2^{n+o(n)}}$.
method: The authors utilize a formal-matrix formalism, mapping the OPB matrix to a multigraph, and developing a two-phase algorithm combining invariant checking with a layered isomorphism search to test equivalence.
model_or_system: The system is an $n$-qubit quantum system, mathematically modeled by an OPB formal matrix $M \in O(n)$. This matrix is associated with an edge-colored complete multigraph $\Gamma(M)$ on $2n$ vertices.
key_observables: The spectrum $\pi(M)$ (part sizes $d_\alpha$), the multiset of column spectra $\{\pi_j(M)\}$, and the multiset of edge multiplicities $\{\mu(r, s)\}$ are key invariants used for comparison.
important_parameters: The number of qubits $n$, the number of variables $v$ (bounded by $2n-1$), and the size of the vertex set $N=2n$.
main_assumptions: The equivalence of two OPB matrices is rigorously proven to be equivalent to the isomorphism of their associated multigraphs.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the multigraph construction for a 3-qubit OPB, and Figure 2 provides a flowchart summarizing the two-phase equivalence-testing algorithm.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the formal-matrix formalism, proves the equivalence theorem linking OPB equivalence to graph isomorphism, derives bounds and asymptotics for the number of classes $a_n$, and concludes with the description and complexity analysis of the two-phase equivalence testing algorithm.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical characterization of quantum state bases and the development of an algorithm to test equivalence are fundamental theoretical tools applicable to understanding quantum resource theories and quantum circuit complexity.
